body: Three family-owned businesses on Brentwood, Missouri's Manchester Road Corridor, Feather-Craft Fly Fishing, Time for Dinner and Convergence Dance and Body Center, along with the owners of the building Feather-Craft leases, sued the city in December 2023 over its designation of their properties as blighted, according to their attorneys, a public-interest firm. The designation would let the city use eminent domain to turn the land over to a private redeveloper. Reason reported that the designation supports a $436 million redevelopment plan and that the city's 2018 blight study by PGAV Planners relied on the corridor's floodplain location and other factors.

In September 2025, after a four-day trial, Judge Kristine Allen Kerr ruled for the city, according to Reason and the plaintiffs' attorneys. She held that 'so long as substantial evidence exists on both sides,' the blight question is 'fairly debatable' and the city's determination stands, and she found the city did not act arbitrarily and capriciously. The court found that an $80 million flood mitigation project completed in 2022 reduced flood risk but did not fully resolve it, according to Reason; the plaintiffs' attorneys describe a $120 million city project to upgrade the streets and mitigate flooding in the corridor.

The plaintiffs' attorneys argue the court applied the wrong standard of review and placed the burden on the plaintiffs, and say the ruling lets the city take 75 properties over conditions like peeling paint and cracked pavement on some of them. Brentwood officials did not respond to Reason's request for comment; the plaintiffs' attorneys said in October 2026 that the city has publicly downplayed the threat of eminent domain. The plaintiffs asked the Missouri Supreme Court to take the case, and on April 21, 2026 it denied their application to transfer it from the Missouri Court of Appeals, Eastern District, according to the court's minutes.

timeline.label: Brentwood hires PGAV Planners to conduct a blight study of the Manchester Road Corridor
The businesses and the building owner sue the City of Brentwood
After a four-day trial, Judge Kristine Allen Kerr upholds the blight designation as "fairly debatable"
The plaintiffs' attorneys announce they will appeal
The Missouri Supreme Court denies the plaintiffs' application to transfer the appeal from the Court of Appeals, Eastern District
